title: A fresh connector registers end to end using a real single-use license key
description: Covers the full bootstrap chain: license key issuance -> CSR generation -> POST /register -> issued client cert -> connector_id/tenant_id recovered from the cert's own CN/OU, matching the identical extraction convention the server uses.
preconditions: A live vtec-management-service with a real CA chain
steps: Issue a license key via POST /license-keys for the test tenant
Start a fresh connector binary configured with that license key and no cached certificate
Observe the connector's startup logs and the resulting connector record
expectedResult: The connector logs 'mTLS identity established' with a real connector_id and tenant_id; GET /connectors shows the new connector with status 'active' after its first heartbeat.

title: A real SQL collection cycle produces decrypted, correct evidence in vtec_evidence_uploads
description: Exercises every link at once: cron fire -> workflow runner -> SQL Collect() against a real Postgres fixture -> credential relayed over WS from Vault -> all 8 synchronous pipeline stages -> JetStream buffer -> Stage 9 upload -> signed envelope -> server-side signature verification -> Vault-resolved decryption key -> Mongo.
preconditions: A registered connector with one SQL adapter targeting a real fixture Postgres instance
The adapter's credential and the tenant encryption key seeded in Vault
steps: Wait for (or trigger) one scheduled collection cycle
Query vtec_evidence_uploads for the resulting document
Decrypt the stored dataBase64 with the same key and decompress with the same zstd library the connector uses
expectedResult: The decrypted, decompressed content matches the real fixture row exactly; checksum verification passes; ucl_controls/masking_applied are set as configured.

title: An adapter's Connect() call successfully resolves its credential via the WS relay to Vault
preconditions: A credential written into Vault at the adapter's exact credential_ref path
steps: Start the connector with an adapter whose credential is not yet cached locally
Observe the credential_request/credential_response envelope exchange over the WS connection
Confirm the adapter's Connect() call succeeds against the real target
expectedResult: The connector never has the raw credential in its own config; it fetches it live via the relay and authenticates successfully to the target.

title: Evidence buffered during a real management-service outage survives and drains fully on reconnect
description: Regression coverage for the Nak hot-loop bug: during the outage, zero Naks should occur (queue not consumed while disconnected); once connectivity returns, every buffered item drains, oldest first.
preconditions: A running connector actively collecting on a short schedule
steps: Stop vtec-management-service for ~50 seconds while the connector keeps collecting
Observe the connector's logs for Nak attempts during the outage
Restart vtec-management-service
Confirm the full backlog drains
expectedResult: Zero Nak attempts occur while disconnected; every item collected during the outage is present in vtec_evidence_uploads after reconnect, with none dead-lettered.

title: Scheduled certificate rotation renews before expiry with zero evidence loss
preconditions: A connector with a short rotation interval configured for test purposes
steps: Let the connector run through at least one full rotation cycle
Confirm the WebSocket client adopts the renewed certificate on its next reconnect
Confirm evidence collection continues uninterrupted across the rotation
expectedResult: The renewed certificate is cached and used; no active connection is forcibly dropped by rotation; no evidence is lost or duplicated across the boundary.

title: Fleet dashboard shows a real registered connector's live status and metrics, not mock data
preconditions: Logged in as a user with vtec.read
At least one real, actively-heartbeating connector registered for the org
steps: Navigate to /vtec/fleet
Compare the displayed status/CPU/memory/queue-depth against the real GET /fleet/health response for the same connector
expectedResult: Every displayed value matches the live API response exactly; no placeholder or hardcoded row is present.

title: The Register Connector modal's issued key and compose snippet actually register a fresh container
preconditions: Logged in as a user with vtec.create
steps: Click 'Register Connector' on /vtec/fleet and issue a key
Copy the displayed docker-compose env block into a fresh Site A compose file
Bring the container up
expectedResult: The container registers successfully using exactly the copied snippet; the new connector appears on /vtec/fleet without a manual page refresh.

title: A credential entered via the Credentials tab is fetched by the live connector and used successfully
description: Full round trip: enter via UI -> stored in Vault (PUT /connectors/{id}/credentials via the vibrantix-backend proxy) -> fetched by the connector via its mTLS relay -> used to complete a real Collect() call against a fixture target.
preconditions: Logged in as a user with vtec.create
A registered connector with an adapter whose credential is not yet cached
steps: Open /vtec/fleet/{connectorId}/credentials and submit a value for the adapter's credential_ref
Trigger (or wait for) that adapter's next collection cycle
Confirm the adapter successfully authenticates and collects
expectedResult: The adapter's Collect() call succeeds using the UI-submitted value; the submitted value never reappears in any subsequent page load or network response body — only a masked reference.

title: A container restart reuses the cached certificate and survives with buffered evidence intact
preconditions: A running, hardened Site A docker-compose deployment (Task 8.1) with evidence buffered from a recent outage
steps: Run docker compose restart on the connector service
Observe the startup logs
Confirm the offline buffer's contents
expectedResult: The connector does NOT re-register (no new license key consumed); it reuses its cached certificate; buffered evidence from before the restart is still present and continues draining normally.

title: A live Prometheus instance shows all 9 §16 series with real, changing values, and VTECConnectorOffline fires within 5 minutes of a killed connector
preconditions: A real Prometheus instance scraping a live, actively-collecting connector using configs/prometheus.yml and configs/prometheus-alerts.yml
steps: Observe vtec_connector_up, vtec_evidence_collected_total, vtec_evidence_upload_bytes_total, vtec_compression_ratio, vtec_pipeline_stage_duration_seconds, vtec_queue_depth, vtec_queue_disk_bytes_used, vtec_adapter_connection_status, and vtec_cert_expiry_seconds over several collection cycles
Kill the connector process outright
Poll Prometheus's /api/v1/alerts every 15s for up to 6 minutes
expectedResult: All 9 series show real values that change across cycles (not static/mocked); VTECConnectorOffline transitions to state 'firing' at approximately the 5-minute mark after the kill.
